### Observed differences

- In the later window, A01 appears exactly once in every trace (200 of 200; mean 1.0 occurrence per trace), whereas it was absent from all 200 earlier traces; it sits near the end of the trace, at a mean relative position of about 0.93. [OCC001, POS001]
- The final segment is rewired around A01: before, 100% of A15's outgoing transitions went to A16 and 100% of A16's went to A15; in the later window A15 splits about 50/50 between A16 and A01, A16 about 51/49 between A01 and A15, and A01 itself leads to A16 (about 54%) and A15 (about 46%). A05 also gained an edge to A01, at about 17% of its outgoing transitions. [DIR011, DIR012, DIR001, DIR005]
- A01 now co-occurs with A15 in every trace, in both orders in near-equal shares (A01 first in about 52 of 100 traces, A15 first in about 48), and the same holds with A16 (about 53/47); earlier these activities never shared a trace. The direct A15→A16 succession fell from 100% to about 63%, with a one-step gap appearing in about 37% of cases; the mirror image holds for A16→A15 (about 65% vs 35%). [REL014, REL015, LAG082, LAG083]
- A02, A06 and A12 became mandatory: each appeared in roughly half of the earlier traces (about 48%, 52% and 52%) but in all 200 later traces; A11 rose from about 26% to about 53% of traces. [OCC002, OCC006, OCC011, OCC012]
- The earlier either/or between A02 and A06 is gone: before, they never occurred in the same trace (A02-only about 48 in 100 traces, A06-only about 52); in the later window they co-occur in every trace, A02's outgoing transitions go to A06 in about 90% of cases (before: A03 about 56%, A07 about 44%), A02 precedes A12 in about 97 of 100 traces (before they were mutually exclusive), and A12 precedes A15/A16 in every trace (before about 52 in 100). [REL019, DIR002, REL025, REL113, REL114]
- Work after A02 runs later: the A02→A03 and A02→A07 gaps grew from 1–2 steps to 3–5 steps, the median positions of A03 and A07 moved from about 0.39/0.40 to about 0.50/0.49 of the trace, and distances from mid-process activities such as A03 and A05 to A15/A16 lengthened by roughly one step. [LAG001, LAG004, POS003, POS007, LAG019, LAG030]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that a new activity, A01, was added at the end of the process, executing once per case in the final segment together with A15 and A16, which previously followed one another directly. The placement is shown directly by relational and positional evidence, not inferred from frequencies alone: A01 went from no occurrences to exactly one in every later trace at a stable late position; A15 and A16 now each route about half of their outgoing transitions to A01 and A01 routes back to both; A01 co-occurs with A15 and A16 in every later trace in mixed order; and the immediate A15→A16 succession dropped from 100% to about 63% while a one-step gap appeared, consistent with A01 occasionally sitting between them. The many agreeing indicators all describe this one underlying difference and are not independent confirmations. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR005, DIR011, DIR012, REL014, REL015, LAG082, LAG083]

Limitations: zero participation in the earlier window only shows A01 was not observed there, so a change in what was recorded cannot be ruled out; and because A01 appears before and after A15 and A16 in similar shares, the evidence supports a terminal cluster containing A01 rather than a single fixed insertion slot. [OCC001, REL014, REL015]

Other differences: A02, A06 and A12, previously each present in about half the traces with A02 and A06 mutually exclusive, now appear in every trace, with A02 leading to A06 in about 90% of its outgoing transitions (previously to A03/A07) and preceding A12 in about 97% of traces; A11's participation roughly doubled (about 26% to 53%); and the A03/A07 block now follows A02 by 3–5 positions instead of 1–2. These participation and routing changes are internally consistent, but the evidence does not establish whether they belong to the same modification as the A01 insertion. [OCC002, OCC006, OCC011, OCC012, REL019, REL025, DIR002, LAG001, LAG004]
